subject: modeling of physical experiments & computer simulations in rstan

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: modeling of physical experiments & computer simulations in rstan
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to combine data from physical experiments and computer simulations within Bayesian framework (desirably using stan modeling language) in order to determine the true model.  The problem is that for some inputs we know that computer simulations (mathematical model) are closer to the truth while for other inputs the experimental data is closer to the truth (mathematical model is not very good).  In the first case we have experimental errors, in the second case we have modeling errors.  For example, at low temperatures mathematical model describes chemical process well while at higher temperatures we trust experiment more (very likely that mathematical model didn't include unknown side reactions).  

One approach to achieve this is through the likelihood (by some kind weighted regression that gives higher weight - lower standard errors - to data at high temperatures).  Not sure how to set that up in Bayesian context, especially within stan framework.  My preference would be using priors but not sure how to do it within stan either.  Does anybody have any suggestions/experience?

Thanks,
Linas

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling of physical experiments & computer simulations in rstan
parts:
Hi, I think the way to go is not to jump to the solution but instead to set up a model with errors.  A simple version would have, for each data point, something like:

y[i] ~ normal (mu[i], sigma[i]);

where mu[i] comes form the model (that is, it would be defined above as mu[i] <- (a + b*x1[i])/(c + d*x2[i]) or whatever your functional form is)
and sigma[i] is set to different parameters corresponding to your knowledge of whether it is a precise or noisy measurement.

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling of physical experiments & computer simulations in rstan
parts:
Andrew,

I would like to add clarification.  In reality the measurement error is the same at low and high temperatures.  Assume for simplicity that input of computer simulation (model mu) is temperature and output of computer simulation is a linear function of temperature.  At low temperatures the true response may be treated as a linear function of temperature (and experimental results follow the line closely).  However at high temperatures the experimental results start deviating from this line significantly.  In this case we believe that true response (concentration) is represented by experimental data (not computer model mu).  My question is how to build model for true concentration based on experimental data and computer model mu.
 
Linas

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] modeling of physical experiments & computer simulations in rstan
parts:
Hi, maybe it would make sense to have a model where the error variance itself varies in a parametric way with temperature?  Or if you’re saying that the curve is still smooth at high temperatures, just nonlinear, it suggests expanding the model to include nonlinear terms, perhaps something parametric if you have a sense of what the curve should look like, or maybe something more flexible like a Gaussian process?
A
